skill.name: ai-music
skill.description: Routes AI music generation and editing requests to RunComfy models, then prepares CLI calls for songs, instrumentals, inpainting, and track extension.
skill.summary: Choose a RunComfy music model and generate or edit audio from a structured brief.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: All 76 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, documentation links, normal token-path disclosure, or model-selection prose. Semantic review found unsafe shell quoting, external transmission of user content, and paid execution without mandatory cost confirmation.

remediation.issue: User-controlled music inputs are embedded in a shell-quoted JSON argument.
remediation.suggestion: Add a structured input-file or standard-input option to the CLI, then update examples to avoid placing user text in shell command strings.

remediation.issue: Prompts, lyrics, and source-audio references are sent to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination and relevant privacy terms, then obtain confirmation before transmitting private, confidential, or licensed content.

remediation.issue: Remote generation can incur charges without a mandatory approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Estimate provider, duration, track count, and cost before execution. Require explicit approval for every batch and any premium model.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Quoting for User-Controlled Music Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The workflow places prompts, lyrics, tags, and URLs inside a single-quoted shell argument. Apostrophes or shell syntax can break quoting before the CLI receives the JSON, contrary to the safety claim.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generic invocation uses a single-quoted inline JSON argument, while line 260 directs the agent to place variable user content in that argument. Shell parsing occurs before the CLI receives JSON.

semantic_findings.title: External Transmission of User Content
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends prompts, lyrics, and source-audio references to the RunComfy Model API. Confidential or licensed material may reach third-party processors without an explicit per-job notice.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly supplies lyrics and audio URLs, and line 254 states that the CLI posts the matching JSON body to the RunComfy Model API.

semantic_findings.title: Paid Generation Without Explicit Cost Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The agent chooses among priced models and invokes remote generation without requiring approval of the provider, duration, or estimated charge. Batch requests could create unintended spend.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill lists per-second prices, routes requests automatically, and says it invokes the selected model. The decision flow contains no mandatory cost confirmation.

content.user_title: Create and Edit AI Music with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Choosing a music model and formatting its inputs can slow production. This skill routes each request and prepares a suitable RunComfy CLI invocation.
actual_capabilities: Selects between ElevenLabs Music, ACE Step, and ACE Step 1.5 based on quality, language, and budget.
Structures prompts, tags, lyrics, duration, and section markers for supported text-to-music endpoints.
Generates vocal songs, instrumentals, jingles, soundtracks, game loops, and background tracks through RunComfy.
Repairs a time-bounded section of existing audio with ACE Step audio inpainting.
Extends existing audio before, after, or in both directions with ACE Step audio outpainting.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated account with sufficient service credits.
Sends prompts and referenced audio to third-party RunComfy and model services.
Does not verify lyric licenses, ownership, commercial rights, or provider-specific usage terms.
Cannot perform mask-based edits; ACE Step editing uses time ranges and limits total duration to four minutes.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Music
use_cases.description: Create a polished jingle or vocal track matched to campaign length, mood, and brand requirements.

use_cases.title: Build Game Audio Libraries
use_cases.description: Generate affordable instrumental loops with varied genres, tempos, and moods for gameplay scenes.

use_cases.title: Repair or Extend Songs
use_cases.description: Replace a weak section or add an intro and outro without regenerating the complete track.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Instrumental
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a {duration}-second instrumental in {genre}. Use {mood}, {tempo}, and {instruments}. Choose a suitable RunComfy model and generate it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new background track.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Vocal Song
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a {duration}-second {language} song in {genre}. Use these lyrics: {lyrics}. Keep the vocal style {vocal_style} and mood {mood}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured song generation with supplied lyrics.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Track Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Repair {start_time} to {end_time} in {audio_url}. Match {style} and replace the section with {section_description}. Preserve the surrounding arrangement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Time-bounded audio inpainting for an existing track.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Music Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan {track_count} tracks for {project_type} and {audience}. Keep within {budget}. Compare models, define varied briefs, estimate cost, and generate only approved tracks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production planning with budget control.

output_examples.input: Create a 30-second upbeat electronic instrumental for a product demonstration.
output: Selected ACE Step base for an affordable instrumental draft.
Prepared tags for upbeat electronic music, steady rhythm, bright synthesizers, and no vocals.
Generated a 30-second track in the requested output directory.

output_examples.input: Replace seconds 20 through 35 of my track with a softer piano bridge.
output: Selected ACE Step audio inpainting for the time-bounded edit.
Kept the source style while specifying a soft piano bridge without drums.
Prepared the repair for seconds 20 through 35.

output_examples.input: Create a polished 10-second vocal jingle for a commercial campaign.
output: Selected ElevenLabs Music for premium vocal quality.
Structured a short campaign brief with vocal direction and section markers.
Presented the estimated cost and generation details for approval.

best_practices: Start with short drafts, then increase duration after the style and arrangement are approved.
State genre, mood, tempo, instruments, vocal language, duration, and section structure explicitly.
Review costs, rights, privacy terms, and service terms before generation, especially for commercial projects.
anti_patterns: Do not place untrusted text directly inside shell-quoted command arguments.
Do not send private audio or lyrics without permission and an approved data-sharing policy.
Do not request paid batches before confirming model, duration, track count, and estimated cost.

faq.question: Which music models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It routes requests to ElevenLabs Music, ACE Step, ACE Step 1.5, and ACE Step audio editing endpoints.

faq.question: Can it create instrumental music?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the genre, mood, instruments, tempo, duration, and that vocals are not required.

faq.question: Can it use my existing audio?
faq.answer: Yes. ACE Step can replace a time range or extend audio before and after the original track.

faq.question: Does it work with multilingual lyrics?
faq.answer: Yes. ACE Step 1.5 supports more than 50 vocal languages, while ElevenLabs Music also supports multilingual vocals.

faq.question: Does generation cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. RunComfy models have usage prices. Confirm the selected model, duration, track count, and estimated cost before execution.

faq.question: Does the skill verify music rights?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify rights for lyrics, source audio, generated outputs, and their intended commercial use.
